The calf head slapped (potentially tried to breach) at least eight times within 20 yards from the boat. The escort dove under the boat and blew bubbles under the water underneath the boat, then he came back up to the surface less than 20 yards from our boat on the starboard side, and did a fluke-up dive about 50 yards away from the boat. The mom and the calf stayed at the surface.

variable_data.general_notes: We saw a school of Spotteds who were milling around at least one HBW. We saw at least one aggressive head lunge towards the dolphins, who were swimming quickly and occasionally leaping. After 5 minutes the dolphins left, and we were quickly mugged by a large adult whale. The whale repeatedly circled under our boat, diving from side to side, and surfaced multiple times within 10 yards of us. Ten minutes into the mugging, a smaller (possibly subadult) whale approached the vessel. The smaller whale turned on her side multiple times, and we were able to see her hemispherical lobe. The larger whale left and the female continued to swim under and around us. We were mugged from 1:55 to 2:35.

variable_data.general_notes:
Comp pod with 3 males 1 female and a calf.  head rises and a lot of fast chasing.  Mom and calf ahead of males "nuzzling" calf rolling around on her head/back slapping its pectoral fins and tail off and on.  One male originally started to move off but then came  back toward the pod before again turning and leaving.  The mom started to pec slap repeatedly.  She kept it up for about 5 minutes straight.  The calf started to tail slap along with her slapping.  One escort remained.  Then a bottlenose dolphin showed up in another whale group near by. They will be logged in the next sighting from OI.

No depth finder onboard to get that data.

variable_data.general_notes: Halfway out to Molokini the captain spotted something about a mile away and when we got closer we saw a small school of bottlenose dolphins foraging. They were jumping out of the water, appearing to chasing prey, and we saw a flyingfish glide about a hundred yards above the surface while fleeing from one of the dolphins. The dolphins also came up close to the boat, seemingly attempting to bow ride, however we were not moving fast enough to create much of a pressure wave for the dolphins to ride in. We saw three adults and one calf and the calf seemed to be foraging as well since it was swimming fast in the water next to an adult animal, and making frequent swift turns in the water. One of the adults had an unusual marking (a elongated light area in the skin) on the right hand side of the dorsal fin.

variable_data.general_notes: This group was behaving very irregularly. One whale was half-spyhopping and sutrfacing a bit off-kilter when it needed to breath. We examined this sighting closely as we suspected the whale could possibly be entangled. The whale "snaked" it's tailstock from one side to the other. We didn't see any line around the peduncle, but the group didn't stray from the spot they were in and didn't dive. No whale lice was observed. Possible hypothesis: labor? 2 other whales milled about at surface, half-spyhopping from time to time. None of us have seen this weird behavior before.

variable_data.general_notes:
Adult spy hopping for a long time 
This adult whale remained with about 2-3 feet of its rostrum above water in a partial spy hop for at least 1.5 with little to no change in behavior. We finally got sight of a small calf pretty light in color next to the whale. It breathed a few times as we watched it but immediately returned to the partial spy hop position.

variable_data.general_notes:
Man of war
Water 82.5 air 27 C
NW 13mph
Depth finder not working, but probably between 20 and 30 ft
Calm
Murky
One group of 4 or 5 met up with another group of 4 or 5, so total we’ve got no more than 10 dolphins. Towards end of sighting, group size increased again … another group from Frankfurt joined and now we have 15 total at least. 
Thought the first group was fishing at first, then they charged toward other group and started playing, then worked their way toward edge of the channel closer to the tiki huts and were surfacing a lot and making variable movements, making me think the moms are teaching their young to fish. Stirring up a lot of sand bear some of the boats too, potentially teaching how to silt net
Nursery group 
Batman, 
No photos 
No other DW boats
4 jet skis passed behind us but didn’t stop to watch them
No cruise ship
Tide dropping 
Waxing gibbous 
29.96 in barometric pressure 
No signs of irritation at us
